title: Vetala Extended Tale 84: The Physician Who Healed the Beggar First
summary: "A master physician named Jivaka was preparing to treat a dying beggar child suffering from acute snakebite when the royal palanquin of the king's wealthy chief minister pulled up....
keywords: vetala extended tale 84: a riddle tale of dharma where vetala tests vikram's sense of justice with story of love, betrayal, and clever decision.
full_text:
Back at the tree, Vikram captured the Vetala and set off again. The Vetala began:

"A master physician named Jivaka was preparing to treat a dying beggar child suffering from acute snakebite when the royal palanquin of the king's wealthy chief minister pulled up. The minister had a painful migraine and offered a pouch of a hundred gold coins for immediate treatment, threatening: 'Attend to me this instant, or you will be driven from this city!'

Jivaka ignored the threats and gold. He stayed focused on the beggar boy, applied the antidote, chanted healing mantras, and stabilized the child's pulse. Only after the boy was breathing safely did Jivaka turn to the minister, saying: 'Your pain is distressing, my lord, but this child had only five minutes to live. A healer's duty is dictated by the imminence of death, not by rank.'

Tell me, Vikram: did the physician act with insolent insubordination, or sacred medical integrity?"

King Vikramaditya replied: "He acted with sacred integrity. The healer's oath is consecrated to life itself. Subordinating a dying child's survival to a nobleman's non-fatal discomfort for gold or fear would have desecrated the divine art of medicine. Jivaka proved himself a true healer of humanity."

"Righteous decision!" cried the Vetala, and soared into the sky.
moral: The sacred duty of healing answers to the urgency of suffering, never to the glitter of gold.
